claims.text: The as-fabricated alloy has composition Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 and was produced by additive manufacturing.
The as-fabricated alloy has an FCC matrix.
High-temperature degradation of this alloy is governed by the evolution and integrity of its surface oxide scale.
Oxygen partial pressure strongly affects oxide-scale evolution in this alloy.
Under oxidizing conditions, the alloy forms a continuous duplex MnCr2O4/Al2O3 scale.
A compact and adherent MnCr2O4/Al2O3 duplex scale suppresses oxygen ingress and metal-cation transport and therefore slows oxidation.
Under low oxygen partial pressure, a thinner MnO-dominated scale forms.
The low-pO2 MnO-dominated scale is porous, discontinuous, poorly adherent, and prone to defects.
Mn is preferentially oxidized and diffuses from the alloy interior to the surface during exposure.
Cr and Al promote protective Cr- and Al-containing oxides, while Mn promotes MnCr2O4 formation and improved scale integrity.
Defects in the low-pO2 scale accelerate inward oxygen transport and elemental depletion.
Accelerated oxygen ingress causes internal oxidation and microcrack formation.
Internal oxidation and microcrack propagation cause accelerated loss of mechanical integrity and eventual catastrophic failure.
Relative to the atmospheric-exposure baseline, high-pO2 exposure delays degradation whereas low-pO2 exposure accelerates mechanical degradation.
The atmospheric-exposure baseline normally develops a protective oxide scale with an expected thickness and composition.
The proposed mechanism applies above approximately 900 °C for exposures of roughly 100 hours or longer, from near-atmospheric oxygen pressure to vacuum or reducing-gas conditions.

contradictions.description: The stated Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 composition contains no Mn, yet the proposed scale and mechanism require preferential oxidation and outward diffusion of Mn and formation of MnO and MnCr2O4. No Mn source, impurity, coating, or composition correction is stated.
